newsitem.title: USA: Political aide Morris signs book contract.
newsitem.headline: Political aide Morris signs book contract.

text.p: President Clinton's former campaign strategist Dick Morris, who resigned last week when a prostitute claimed he told her political secrets, has signed a deal to write a book, Random House publishers said Thursday.

Random House president Harold Evans said in a statement that Morris "has had a unique experience. He possesses one of the most brilliant political minds I've ever encountered and has insight into politics and the White House that readers will find fascinating."

The statement said the book, to be published after the November presidential election, would cover Morris' two years as Clinton's chief political strategist. The company did not disclose how much Morris would be paid.

Call-girl Sherry Rowlands alleged in this week's Star supermarket tabloid that Morris hired her at $200-an-hour weekly for almost a year and gave her information confidential to the White House inner circle.

She has denied that anyone in the Republican Party had any hand in the story, which appeared in the New York Post the day Clinton delivered his acceptance speech to the Democratic convention in Chicago.

Rowlands, whom Star editors said had contacted them in July, told the magazine Morris, 48 and married, bragged and showed her high-level speeches, revealed policy changes and let her eavesdrop on a telephone conversation with Clinton.
Morris, who first worked with Clinton on his 1977 Arkansas gubernatorial campaign, has also teamed up with Republicans such as Senate Majority leader Trent Lott and California Gov. Pete Wilson.
